# pflow.xyz — Explanations you can run

LLM-written code got good in the last year, and understanding it didn't get
faster. You can only move as fast as you comprehend what you've built. pflow
turns each model into something you can see, run and check, with proofs and
provenance attached. Under the hood every model is a Petri net, so runs replay
and proofs check.

A comprehension, in the programmer's sense, builds a thing from its description.
pflow does that for systems: describe it, and get a model you can run, check and
understand.

pflow.xyz is a visual editor and simulator with an embeddable, dependency-free ES
module library for discrete simulation and continuous (ODE) analysis. All
modules are served from this origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so
they can be imported directly from any ad-hoc HTML page — no build step, no
npm.

## Modules (import these URLs directly)

- https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js — mass-action ODE solver (Tsit5, adaptive)
  plus SVGPlotter, an interactive SVG line/scatter plotter.
  Exports: fromJSON, setState, setRates, ODEProblem, ODESolution, Tsit5,
  solve, SVGPlotter, Place, Transition, Arc, PetriNet.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-sim.js — discrete firing semantics (pure functions).
  Exports: enabled, fire, enabledTransitions, marking, getArcWeight,
  capacityOf.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-colors.js — colored-net unfolding (expandColors,
  expandState). petri-solver.js imports it automatically.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.js — the full `<petri-view>` editor web
  component (drag-and-drop editing, discrete play mode, tabbed Analysis
  workbench: ODE simulate / rate scan / sweep / phase plot).
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.css — editor styles (design tokens, light +
  dark via prefers-color-scheme).
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-learn.js — differentiable fitting for Petri-net ODE
  models: a JS mirror of go-pflow's `learn` package. Forward sensitivities
  (`LearnableProblem.solveWithSensitivities`, augmented ODE with analytic
  Jacobian) and reverse-mode/adjoint sensitivities
  (`LearnableProblem.solveAdjoint`, one backward solve — the tool for a rate
  function with many parameters, at a cost independent of parameter count).
  Exports: `LearnableProblem`, `ScalarRateFunc`, `SharedScalar` (tied
  parameters), `mseLossGrad`/`relativeMseLossGrad`/`mseLossAdjoint`/
  `relativeMseLossAdjoint`, `adamMinimize`/`nelderMead`/`coordinateDescent`,
  `hingeRankLoss`, `fit`/`fitGradient`/`fitRates` (the no-boilerplate
  entry point: fit per-transition scalar rates to observed trajectories).
  petri-solver.js's bytes are untouched by this module.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-ssa.js — portable Gillespie SSA (discrete-stochastic
  simulation), byte-exact with go-pflow, pflow-rs and pflow-jl via a fixed
  PRNG (SplitMix64 → xoshiro256**) and a ported log; no dependency on the
  other modules. `simulate(model, {horizon, samples, realizations, seed})` →
  `{ places, times, series: {id: {values, stddev}}, final }` (ensemble
  mean/stddev/final per place). Exports: splitmix64, Xoshiro256, plog,
  combinations, compile, simulate.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-sde.js — chemical Langevin SDE, the third leg of
  Petri.jl's ODEProblem/JumpProblem/SDEProblem trio: continuous state via
  Euler-Maruyama, but with the net's own intrinsic firing noise rather than
  SSA's discrete events or the ODE's none at all. Reuses petri-ssa.js's
  compile(), Xoshiro256 and plog rather than duplicating them.
  `simulateSDE(model, {horizon, samples, realizations, seed})` → the same
  shape as simulate(), plus `diverged`/`reason`/`caveats` when the model
  gates (read arc, inhibitor, reached capacity — none has a continuous
  analogue). Exports: GaussianSampler, combinationsReal, simulateSDE,
  CHEMICAL_LANGEVIN_ASSUMPTION. Not yet part of the byte-exact
  cross-language contract SSA has — its Gaussian sampler is checked
  bit-for-bit against go-pflow's own reference vectors, but the ensemble
  output is checked only for consistency against this module's own SSA.

Which one for which question: petri-solver.js's ODE has no firing instant,
so it cannot express a read arc, an inhibitor, a reached capacity or a
guard — the go-pflow reference implementation refuses a model that has any
of these rather than silently ignore them, and this module's semantics
match it. petri-sde.js refuses the same way, for the same reason. Use
petri-ssa.js for a gated model, or whenever token counts are small enough
that variance is the answer rather than noise around it; use petri-sde.js
when you want that noise without individual discrete events (large
populations, continuous-state tooling that still needs the fluctuation).
Above input-arc weight 1 all three rate laws diverge genuinely (mass
action multiplies each input's concentration in once regardless of
weight; SSA's and the SDE's propensity use the full combinatorial
C(m, weight) term, continuous in the SDE's case) — not a bug in any of
them, a different question. Full rules with a worked example:
docs/engine-selection.md (vendored from go-pflow, scripts/docs-sync.sh
check/sync).

The ODE semantics are behaviorally identical to go-pflow
(github.com/pflow-xyz/go-pflow) — enforced by a differential parity test
suite — so browser results match server-side analysis.

## Model format (JSON-LD)

```json
{
  "@context": "https://pflow.xyz/schema",
  "@type": "PetriNet",
  "@version": "1.1",
  "token": ["https://pflow.xyz/tokens/black"],
  "places": {
    "water":  { "@type": "Place", "initial": [10], "capacity": [0], "x": 60,  "y": 60 },
    "coffee": { "@type": "Place", "initial": [0],  "capacity": [0], "x": 260, "y": 60 }
  },
  "transitions": {
    "brew": { "@type": "Transition", "x": 160, "y": 60 }
  },
  "arcs": [
    { "@type": "Arrow", "source": "water", "target": "brew", "weight": [1] },
    { "@type": "Arrow", "source": "brew", "target": "coffee", "weight": [1] }
  ]
}
```

Notes: `capacity` 0 or absent means unbounded. `initial`, `capacity`, and
`weight` are vectors — one entry per token color in `token`; an explicit 0
weight component means "this color is not involved". Set
`"inhibitTransition": true` on an arc for an inhibitor.

## Sandboxed environments (strict-CSP hosts)

**claude.ai artifacts cannot load these modules today.** Artifact CSP allows
external scripts only from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`; imports from pflow.xyz,
jsDelivr, esm.sh, or unpkg are all refused there and fail with
`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`. Don't write a fallback loader
for artifacts — it fails on every origin. Host the page elsewhere (any static
host works; the modules are CORS-open). A cdnjs submission is staged; once
accepted, `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/pflow-xyz/<version>/petri-solver.js`
will be the artifact-compatible URL — until then that URL 404s.

Also: `file://` pages can't load ES modules at all (CORS blocks them), so
"open the HTML file in a browser" is not enough for local use — serve it,
e.g. `python3 -m http.server`.

For *other* strict-CSP hosts that do allow common CDNs, jsDelivr mirrors the
repo; relative imports (petri-colors.js) resolve against whichever origin
loaded the module, so either source is self-sufficient:

```js
const pf = await import("https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js")
  .catch(() => import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@v1.27.0/public/petri-solver.js"));
```

Pin a release tag (as above) or commit SHA — `@main` is cached ~12h by
jsDelivr, so it lags the latest deploy. `@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz` has been on npm
since 2026-08-01, so npm-backed CDNs work too:
`https://esm.sh/@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@1.27.0/petri-solver.js` or
`https://unpkg.com/@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@1.27.0/petri-solver.js` (same paths
work for petri-learn.js, petri-sim.js, etc. — see package.json's `exports`
map). cdnjs listing is pending (needs 800+ npm downloads/month or 200 GitHub
stars).

## Minimal ad-hoc page: solve an ODE and plot it

```html
<div id="plot"></div>
<script type="module">
  const pf = await import("https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js")
    .catch(() => import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@v1.27.0/public/petri-solver.js"));

  const model = { /* JSON-LD model as above */ };
  const net = pf.fromJSON(model);
  const prob = new pf.ODEProblem(net, pf.setState(net), [0, 10],
                                 pf.setRates(net, { brew: 0.5 }));
  const sol = pf.solve(prob, pf.Tsit5(), { dt: 0.01, abstol: 1e-6, reltol: 1e-3, adaptive: true });

  const plot = pf.SVGPlotter.plotSolution(sol, ["water", "coffee"], {
    title: "Brew kinetics", xlabel: "Time", ylabel: "Tokens", width: 720, height: 400,
  });
  document.getElementById("plot").innerHTML = plot.svg;
  plot.setupInteractivity();   // crosshair, tooltip, click-to-toggle legend
  console.log(sol.getFinalState());
</script>
```

The emitted SVG uses `var(--pv-viz-*, lightFallback)` colors: it renders the
validated light palette standalone, and follows the host theme if the page
defines those custom properties (petri-view.css does).

## Minimal ad-hoc page: full editor

```html
<script type="module" src="https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.css">
<petri-view data-json-editor>
  <script type="application/ld+json">{ /* JSON-LD model */ }</script>
</petri-view>
```

## Discrete simulation

```js
import * as sim from "https://pflow.xyz/petri-sim.js";
sim.enabledTransitions(model);        // -> ["brew"]
const marks = sim.fire(model, "brew"); // -> {"water":[9],"coffee":[1]} or null
```

`fire` is pure: pass the returned marking back as the third argument to step
again.

## MCP server

`https://pflow.xyz/mcp` runs these tools on the server, on the net or
composition passed in the call. Setup and every tool: https://pflow.xyz/mcp.html

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pflow https://pflow.xyz/mcp
```

Any other client: it is stateless Streamable HTTP, so POST JSON-RPC to the URL;
there is no event stream. Only `pflow_save` needs a sign-in, and saved nets are
public.

```bash
curl -s https://pflow.xyz/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

**Nets:** pflow_edit, pflow_info, pflow_check, pflow_validate, pflow_verify,
pflow_fire, pflow_reachability, pflow_invariants, pflow_incidence,
pflow_simulate, pflow_ssa, pflow_sde, pflow_what_if, pflow_rate_scan,
pflow_optimize, pflow_cid, pflow_get, pflow_export, pflow_links, pflow_save,
pflow_artifact (an interactive page of the net, to publish as an Artifact).

**Two-sided games:** exact alpha-beta search over the firing rule, on a net whose
moves belong to two sides. The net's marking is the position.

- pflow_game_value: the position's value with both sides playing perfectly, from
  the +1 side's view.
- pflow_game_move: a best move and the value. The move is not played.

Both need `net`, `sides` (transition-id prefix to sign) and `reward` (place to
weight, read from the final marking). `auto` names transition-id prefixes that
fire before anyone chooses; `plan`, `nodes` and `book` tune the search. Past the
node budget the answer is `exact: false` with a null value.

Nim with a pile of 3, where each side takes 1 or 2 and a side left with no move
has lost. The side that moves first loses, so the value is -1:

```json
{"name": "pflow_game_value", "arguments": {
  "sides": {"a_": 1, "b_": -1},
  "reward": {"b_turn": 1, "a_turn": -1},
  "net": {
    "@context": "https://pflow.xyz/schema", "@type": "PetriNet",
    "places": {
      "pile": {"initial": [3], "capacity": [0]},
      "a_turn": {"initial": [1], "capacity": [0]},
      "b_turn": {"initial": [0], "capacity": [0]}
    },
    "transitions": {"a_take1": {}, "a_take2": {}, "b_take1": {}, "b_take2": {}},
    "arcs": [
      {"source": "pile", "target": "a_take1", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "a_turn", "target": "a_take1", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "a_take1", "target": "b_turn", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "pile", "target": "a_take2", "weight": [2]},
      {"source": "a_turn", "target": "a_take2", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "a_take2", "target": "b_turn", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "pile", "target": "b_take1", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "b_turn", "target": "b_take1", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "b_take1", "target": "a_turn", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "pile", "target": "b_take2", "weight": [2]},
      {"source": "b_turn", "target": "b_take2", "weight": [1]},
      {"source": "b_take2", "target": "a_turn", "weight": [1]}
    ]
  }
}}
```

**Compositions:** a `PetriNetBundle` is subnets, the ports on their boundaries
and typed links between them (token, data, event, guard). The bundle travels in
the call and nothing is stored.

- pflow_bundle_example: a composition to start from (an order queue, a worker
  pool and a payment saga), with its catalog and four scenarios.
- pflow_bundle_validate: check the subnets, then every link. Errors name the link
  as `links[i]`.
- pflow_bundle_candidates: the links a port could take, each with its verdict.
  Only declared ports count here; a subnet with no `ports` array offers none.
- pflow_bundle_add_link: add a link if it is legal; a refusal gives the reasons.
  It takes `kind`, `from` and `to` only, as `"subnet:port"`.
- pflow_bundle_flatten: one flat net, with maps back to the subnets.
- pflow_bundle_run: fire a `script` or one of the example's `scenario`s, and check
  what it expects. A script member is the transition's own id in its subnet
  (`payment/do_charge`), not the port id a link names (`do:charge`).
- pflow_bundle_incidence: the flat net's incidence matrix, and whether each
  declared constraint is a conservation law of the composition.

A usual order: pflow_bundle_example, then pflow_bundle_candidates with
`{"bundle": ..., "from": "orders:dequeue", "only_ok": true}`, then
pflow_bundle_add_link, pflow_bundle_validate and
`pflow_bundle_run` with `{"bundle": ..., "scenario": "refund"}`.

The flat net is not a pflow.xyz net: pflow_simulate, pflow_fire and the other net
tools cannot read it, so fire it with pflow_bundle_run. Give every arc an explicit
weight: an arc with none fires as 1 but counts as 0 in a subnet's incidence block.

A failed `expect` in a run's answer is a finding about the composition, not a tool
error. The example's `refund` and `charge-fails` both leave a worker out of the
pool, and its `second-order` stops at a transition that cannot fire.

## Related services

- POST https://pflow.xyz/api/svg — render a model to SVG server-side.
- GET  https://pflow.xyz/schema — the JSON-LD @context.
- https://ontology.pflow.xyz — the formal ontology behind that @context: terms,
  glossary concepts and the pflow software components. Downloads
  (Turtle, JSON-LD, N-Triples, RDF/XML, with SHA256SUMS), a read-only SPARQL
  endpoint at `/sparql` and an MCP server at `/mcp`.
- https://sim.pflow.xyz/mcp — sim MCP server (JSON-RPC): build, run and
  check models (sim_create_model, sim_scenario, sim_invariants, sim_reach,
  sim_verify, …).
- https://book.pflow.xyz — the book on modeling with Petri nets.
- https://sim.pflow.xyz — describe a process, get a model you can run
  and check: store a model with one POST, then seeded scenario comparison,
  invariants and reachability proofs, calibration against event logs, and
  diagnostics that rank every knob by measured influence on the objective.
  MCP server at `https://sim.pflow.xyz/mcp`.
- https://github.com/pflow-xyz/pflow-native — native desktop editor and
  simulator for the same JSON-LD models (pflow-rs), with a CLI and an MCP
  server (`pflow-native-cli mcp`).
